To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in the large depth and width limit the spectrum of NNGP and NTK kernels are ``weakly data dependent'', and that this allows us to characterize the trainability and generalizability of neural networks as functions of their hyperparameters.

1) In the wide network limit at large depths, the spectrum of the Neural Tangent and Neural Network Gaussian Process kernels simplify considerably, 2) The spectrum of these kernels is a function of the hyperparameters of the network and 3) By analyzing this spectrum one can precisely determine whether the network will train and generalize.

(1) the NNGP is the kernel describing random wide networks, (2) the NTK is the kernel describing gradient descent training of the same, (3) in the wide network and large depth limit, the spectrum of the two kernels simplify considerably and become weakly data-dependent, and (4) this simplification allows us to precisely predict trainability and generalizability of wide neural networks across a range of network architectures and hyperparameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental question of trainability and the generalization performance of deep learning.
the fundamental question of trainability and generalize of neural networks.
a fundamental question in deep learning: how to design networks that can be trained to generalize to novel data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in the large depth and wide width limit the trainability of a deep network depends solely on its spectrum, and its generalization performance on the spectrum and the data distribution.

(i) for large depth, the NTK and NNGP are weakly data-dependent and their eigenvalue spectra are well described by simple analytical expressions, (ii) the spectrum of the trainability kernel is identical to that of the NTK, (iii) the spectrum of trainability kernel is the same as that of the test kernel in the case of FCNs and CNNs without global average pooling,
the NTK theory is correct and that it is a powerful tool for the analysis of the trainability and generalizability of neural networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spectrum of the Neural Tangent kernel provides a complete and accurate characterization of trainability, generalization, and the learning dynamics of wide neural networks in the limit of infinite depth and large widths.
in the large depth, wide network limit the spectrum of kernels governing random and trained networks are both data-independent.
the NTK and NNGP kernels provide a simple and powerful framework to understand the behavior of wide neural networks in the large depth regime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in the wide and deep regime, trainability and generalizability are determined by a single hyperparameter, the ratio of the width of the network to the number of examples.
the large depth limit is a powerful theoretical tool that can help us understand the training and generalization properties of deep networks.
trainability and generalizability of deep networks are intimately linked and that the NTK and NNGP kernels are the key tools in understanding the behavior of deep networks in the large depth regime.
